summary: When the work is done in {place}, the contracts show who actually got a share.
realLife: By 1980 minority firms had performed roughly a quarter of Atlanta’s airport expansion work after Jackson pressed for their inclusion.
gates: A public project with participation commitments has reached closeout.
weights: Disputed invoices increase the likelihood that staff reopen the accounting.
inGame: needs: participation by firm in completed contracts.

turns.what: A promised subcontract never reaches the firm.
turns.pulledBy: The prime contractor keeps the work in house.
turns.writesBack: The closeout shows a gap between promised and paid participation.

turns.what: A subcontractor is credited after an invoice review.
turns.pulledBy: Its payment was missing from the first accounting.
turns.writesBack: The corrected closeout names the firm and amount.
